author: Helen Keller
title: The Story of My Life
edition: New York: Doubleday, Page & Company, 1905. Part I, Helen Keller’s memoir, in the University of Pennsylvania A Celebration of Women Writers transcription of that dated edition. HTML emphasis markup and illustrations omitted; prose whitespace normalized and original verse line breaks retained. This is not the unidentified Project Gutenberg print exemplar. Editorial footnote markers and cross-reference notes omitted; inset verse retained. One transcription error corrected to the Doubleday, Page print: “The two stories were so much alike” (chapter XIV; Internet Archive storyofmylife00kell, 1903, and storymylife00sullgoog, 1905). The library text holds the whole 1905 book: Part I (the memoir), Part II (her letters, 1887-1901, with John Albert Macy's introduction and connecting notes) and Part III (Macy's supplementary account, quoting Anne Mansfield Sullivan's letters and reports) and the editor's notes (which the transcription gathers at the end of the book); the editor's preface is omitted. The nightly excerpts omit the note reference numbers, which the library text keeps. Part I chapters IV and XXIII (pages 21–24 and 132–140) were collated word by word against the 1905 print (storymylife00sullgoog; its OCR text, after whitespace normalisation, with every difference decided on the page image, and the 1903 print agreeing) on 2026-11-18, and twelve transcription errors corrected to it: “immeasurable contrast,” “no strong sentiment or tenderness” and “the close of that eventful day” (chapter IV); “frosty finger-tips,” “In spite of the lapse of years,” “I remember well the first time,” “He had invited,” “just after I had learned to speak,” “helped us over many rough places,” “by means of which he expects to discover,” “Mrs. William Thaw” and “guides vast enterprises” (chapter XXIII); one existing reading (the Grade 7 calendar reading of chapter IV) changed. Part I chapter XXII (pages 119–131) was collated the same way on 2026-11-18 and nine transcription errors corrected to the print: “have evidence of things unseen,” “lakes and woods, and broad,” “the happy-go-lucky way I love,” “manoeuvers,” “It there are children around” (the print’s own misprint for “If,” in the 1903 print too, kept as printed), “the wingéd hours,” “O dark, dark, dark,” “the wonderful rhythmical flow” and “until I could say it”; no existing reading changed.

rights.basis: Original English memoir in the explicitly dated 1905 Doubleday, Page edition transcribed by the University of Pennsylvania library. The title page and library bibliographic statement identify 1905; this publication is more than 95 years before 2026 and is public domain in the United States.

acquisition.method: UPenn A Celebration of Women Writers HTML (life.html). Kept the dedication, the whole body from PART I, and the editor's NOTES: Part I, Part II with its introduction and letters, Part III. Removed the site header and footer, title page, copyright leaf, editor's preface, contents, list of illustrations, illustration captions and images, page counters, and the transcription's [Page N] labels in the notes section. Each footnote reference becomes [n] (the transcription's numbering) placed directly after the preceding text; the notes follow the book after a NOTES. paragraph label, each as [Footnote n: text] (note 32, which quotes verse, runs over a paragraph, a stanza and a paragraph, the bracket closing on the last). Each P is one paragraph with whitespace collapsed (BR as a space; letter titles, addresses, closings and signatures stay separate paragraphs); a verse BLOCKQUOTE is one stanza with BR as line breaks and the HTML's other whitespace collapsed to single spaces (so continuation lines keep one leading space); H3 headings become headings (parts level 1, chapters and sections level 2; the running title before Chapter I dropped); table rows are tab-separated paragraphs; italics are not marked. The declared emendation (we to were, chapter XIV) is applied before conversion. The emendations from the 2026-11-18 collation of chapters IV and XXIII (see edition) are applied to the converted text. The emendations from the 2026-11-18 collation of chapter XXII (see edition) are applied the same way. In Part III, the line listing its chapter titles (contents) was removed and the missing heading CHAPTER II PERSONALITY restored before "Miss Keller is tall and strongly built" on 2026-11-18.
